summary: PulseLink is health-monitoring software for astronauts on surface EVA. A sensor liner inside the EVA glove measures pulse, SpO2, skin temperature, and motion, so every routine suit interaction a hatch, a tool, a checklist tap doubles as a Fit-to-Go health check. The glove sends a signed decision, not raw biometrics: a deterministic chain checks proximity, pulse, gesture, and a nonce before the secure element signs. Replayed or spoofed signals are denied. A planned advisory-only AI layer can recommend rest or flag a block, but it holds no key and never authorizes; if a model fails, fixed NASA-derived thresholds keep the console working. A flight-surgeon console shows the Fit-to-Go decision (demo: AMBER, risk 0.478; HR 148 / limit 150), the top contributing factors, the trust chain, and a hash-chained mission log. The demo uses cached NASA DONKI and POWER snapshots plus configurable HRP/LSDA-derived thresholds; glove vitals are simulated and labeled. The suit is shown as platform context the deliverable is the glove and software. Concept, TRL 3–5.
